name: Mary
bio: John's Gospel names a Mary, wife of Cleophas, standing by the cross alongside Jesus's mother and Mary Magdalene, traditionally identified with this same Mary, mother of James and Joses (John 19:25). Mary, mother of James and Joses, was among the women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and watched his crucifixion from a distance, later keeping vigil at his tomb (Matthew 27:55-61). She is a different figure from Mary, the mother of Jesus. At dawn on the first day of the week, she and Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and were met by an angel announcing Jesus's resurrection, and then by the risen Jesus himself (Matthew 28:1-10). Mark's account of the crucifixion identifies her son as "James the less" (Mark 15:40). Luke names her, along with Mary Magdalene and Joanna, as one of the women who found the empty tomb, met two angels, and reported the news to the apostles, who dismissed it as nonsense (Luke 24:1-11).
